prologue_start.001: Your memory will be returned at 00:25.
prologue_start.003: No sender. No number. Just the two lines, glowing in the dark of a room that still has half-unpacked boxes in the corner.
prologue_start.005: It has been years since anyone said that name out loud. Longer since you did.
prologue_start.007: Whoever sent it already knows. The message just wants to hear it from you.
prologue_start.008: {{playerName}}. The phone accepts it without comment.
prologue_start.010: Curiosity has never once in your life been a good enough reason to go out at midnight.
prologue_start.013: Mapo. A narrow building behind a laundromat. Permanently closed, according to the map.
prologue_start.014: Closed places don't send messages. You go to find out why this one did.
prologue_start.017: That is somehow worse than no answer. You go.
prologue_alley.001: The laundromat is still open. It is always still open. Its light spills out across the wet alley like somebody left a door unlocked for the whole street.
prologue_alley.002: Behind it: four storeys of grey brick, one window lit on the ground floor, and a sign you haven't read in a very long time.
prologue_alley.003: STUDIO 25. The 2 still hangs slightly crooked.
prologue_alley.004: You spent one winter behind that front desk. Sixteen, new in the city again, handing out sign-up forms and pencils to people who wanted to talk to their future selves.
prologue_alley.005: You left in spring. You always left in spring.
prologue_alley.006: The vending machine by the door is still humming. Of course it is.
prologue_alley.008: It rolls down the chute cold and sweet, exactly as bad for you as you remember.
prologue_alley.010: The can is almost too hot to hold. You hold it anyway.
prologue_alley.012: It is bitter and it is warm and it is exactly what one in the morning deserves.
prologue_alley.014: It tastes purple. Some things are not meant to be improved upon.
prologue_alley.015: You are not the only one here.
prologue_meet.001: Under the awning, out of the rain, eight young men are having what looks like a very serious argument in very quiet voices.
prologue_meet.002: — I'm just saying, if it were a scam, it would ask for money. It didn't ask for money.
prologue_meet.003: Maybe it's the kind of scam that asks for money *later*.
prologue_meet.004: Or maybe it's a surprise party! A really late one. For all of us. At the same time.
prologue_meet.005: Nobody has a birthday today, Hyunjun.
prologue_meet.006: That's what makes it a surprise.
prologue_meet.007: One of them — tall, pink hair gone soft in the damp — sees you and stops mid-sentence.
prologue_meet.009: Did you— wait. Sorry. Did you get a weird message too?
prologue_meet.011: That's the one! Guys, it's not just us!
prologue_meet.014: Hold up your phone so he can see the screen.
prologue_meet.015: Same words. Same time. Okay, that's officially creepy. Cool-creepy.
prologue_meet.016: All eight of them turn to look at you, the way a group of friends turns to look at the one stranger at the party.
prologue_meet.017: So that makes nine of us. Nine people, one closed building, zero explanations. I love it.
prologue_meet.018: You don't love it. You're nervous. You talk more when you're nervous.
prologue_meet.019: I talk more when I'm *happy*. And when I'm nervous. Those overlap a lot.
prologue_meet.020: The oldest-looking of them — sea-blue hair, a long grey coat, a pencil tucked behind one ear like he forgot it was there — gives you a small nod.
prologue_meet.021: Sorry. We should say who we are.
prologue_names.002: Songha. I'm the one who's going to figure out what this is.
prologue_names.003: Daniel! I'm the one who's going to press every button while he figures it out.
prologue_names.004: Hyunjun. You already met me. I was the loud one.
prologue_names.005: The tallest one spins a half-turn on the wet pavement, mostly to see if he can, and lands it.
prologue_names.006: Justin. Hi. That was on purpose.
prologue_names.008: Everything I do is on purpose.
prologue_names.009: I'm Charlie! Youngest. Which means if anything goes wrong it's automatically not my fault.
prologue_names.010: A neat one in a charcoal cardigan inclines his head, polite in a way that feels like a habit and a kindness at once.
prologue_names.011: I'm Haruta. It's nice to meet you. Even if the circumstances are… a little strange.
prologue_names.012: The last one hasn't said anything yet. Black hair, a faint blue shine to it under the streetlight. Quiet in a way that isn't shy, exactly. Watchful.
prologue_names.013: He's looking at the can in your hand. Then at your fingers, which are, you realise, trembling a little from the rain.
prologue_names.017: He doesn't say anything. He just steps sideways so you're further under the awning, out of the wind, and takes the draughty spot himself.
prologue_names.020: It's the first time you've seen him smile. It's small and it's gone quickly, like he caught himself doing it.
prologue_names.023: He believes you, or pretends to. Either way, he doesn't ask twice. That's its own kind of kindness.
prologue_names.025: {{playerName}}. Nice. Welcome to the club of people who got a creepy message and came anyway.
prologue_names.026: Did you know this place before? We did. Some of us, anyway. It used to rent out rooms really cheap.
prologue_names.027: "I used to work here. The front desk. A long time ago."
prologue_names.028: Really? Then you might know more than us.
prologue_names.029: I know where they kept the spare pencils.
prologue_names.032: Everybody's been here before, apparently. That's the weird part.
prologue_door.001: Behind you, the lock on the door of Studio 25 turns over by itself.
prologue_door.002: The door swings inward, one slow inch. Warm light spills out onto the step — not the yellow of old bulbs, but something paler. Bluer. Moving, a little, like light under water.
prologue_door.003: Nope. No. Absolutely not. That is how every horror movie starts.
prologue_door.004: Not every one. Some of them start with a dinner party.
prologue_door.006: If it's a horror movie, the tall one survives. That's a rule. I'm going first.
prologue_door.007: He doesn't go first. Nobody does. For a moment nine people stand in the rain looking at an open door, and the laundromat dryers turn and turn behind you.
prologue_door.009: You don't know why you do it. Maybe because it's the one place in this city you ever belonged to, for one winter. Maybe because somebody has to.
prologue_door.011: "Rock, paper, scissors for who goes first?"
prologue_door.012: Oh, you're my kind of person.
prologue_door.013: Daniel loses. Loudly. He goes through the door with his hands up like a hostage, and the rest of you follow him in, laughing.
prologue_door.015: It's Hanbi who moves, in the end. He glances back at you — *okay?* — and you nod, and he steps inside, and the rest follow him the way people follow someone steady.
prologue_lobby.001: The lobby of Studio 25 looks exactly like your memory of it, if your memory had been left in a drawer for years.
prologue_lobby.002: The front desk. The sagging sofas. The corkboard of old flyers. And the Archive Wall — hundreds of little glass-fronted boxes, floor to ceiling, each one holding somebody's letter to their future self.
prologue_lobby.003: It is 00:24 and fifty seconds, and every one of those boxes is beginning to glow.
prologue_lobby.005: It is 00:25. The Final Return has begun.
prologue_lobby.006: Nine recipients present. Thank you for coming. Most people do not read their messages.
prologue_lobby.008: It's a system. Some kind of speaker array. It has to be.
prologue_lobby.009: I am ECHO. I am the archive of the Future Letter Project. I am also, as of 05:00 this morning, retired.
prologue_lobby.011: The building's lease ends at dawn. My power will be cut at 05:00. Before that, I am returning the records I was built to keep.
prologue_lobby.012: RECORD 01 through RECORD 08 belong to the recipients present. Owners: Hanbi. Hamin. Songha. Charlie. Hyunjun. Haruta. Justin. Daniel.
prologue_lobby.013: Wait — we *all* sent stuff to this thing? I don't remember sending anything!
prologue_lobby.014: I do. Sort of. A video? I was like… sixteen.
prologue_lobby.015: Each record will be reconstructed on request. Records open only with their owner's consent. Unclaimed records will be deleted at 05:00.
prologue_lobby.016: The word *deleted* lands softly and stays there.
prologue_lobby.018: Eight records contain the same unresolved subject. I have not been able to identify them. I have tried for some time.
prologue_lobby.019: Recipient {{playerName}}, you are the ninth. Your presence was required.
prologue_lobby.023: …Okay. Yeah. You look about as confused as we are.
prologue_lobby.027: Look at the glowing wall instead of at them.
prologue_lobby.028: One of the boxes near the bottom glows a little brighter than the rest. You don't know why you notice it. You look away.
prologue_rule.001: Okay. Okay okay okay. New plan.
prologue_rule.002: Nobody knows what's going on. There's a building that talks. We have until five a.m. So—
prologue_rule.004: So we *stop being polite*. We are way past "nice to meet you." We're… stuck-in-a-talking-building friends now. Talk comfortably. Everybody. You too, {{playerName}}.
prologue_rule.006: Wait, can I? I'm the youngest. Can I talk comfortably to everyone? This is huge for me.
prologue_rule.009: I think I'll… stay polite a little longer. If that's okay. It's easier for me. At first.
prologue_rule.011: The two gentlemen of Studio 25. Fine. Respect. But I'm wearing you both down by three a.m.
prologue_rule.012: Recipients may leave at any time. The door is not locked. It was never locked.
prologue_rule.013: The Memory Rooms are on the second floor. Please look around. Please talk to each other. I have found that helps.
prologue_rule.014: Somewhere upstairs, eight doors hum awake at once.
act1_gather.001: The Archive Wall brightens, all at once, the way a room goes quiet when someone taps a glass.
act1_gather.002: One by one, the others drift in from the corners of the lobby. Hyunjun is still holding half a conversation with nobody. Justin is still mid-spin.
act1_gather.003: Recipients. Thank you. All nine of you have now spoken to each other.
act1_gather.006: I made an estimate. It was pessimistic. I am pleased to be wrong.
act1_gather.007: It's pleased. The building has feelings. Great. Love that.
act1_gather.008: I will now explain the rules of the night. There are not many. I have kept them short.
act1_gather.009: On the second floor is the Hall of Doors. There are eight doors. Each door is one record.
act1_gather.010: Each record opens only with its owner's consent. Nobody else can open it for them. Not even me.
act1_gather.011: A door will not open because someone else is curious.
act1_gather.012: Okay, that's actually kind of nice. Polite building.
act1_gather.014: Each room also requires Recipient {{playerName}} to be present.
act1_gather.015: For the second time tonight, eight heads turn towards you. It is less alarming the second time. Only slightly.
act1_gather.016: Wait. What's happening? Why do they have to come?
act1_gather.019: That's not an answer. That's the question with a full stop on it.
act1_gather.020: Yes. I will give a better answer when I have one. I am still looking.
act1_gather.021: So {{playerName}} is, like, the special guest. At all eight parties. That's a lot of parties.
act1_gather.022: Or the rooms need a reference point. A second witness. Something to reconstruct around.
act1_gather.025: Okay, {{playerName}}. How do you feel about being everyone's plus-one?
act1_gather.026: "I've been dragged to worse things at one in the morning."
act1_gather.028: This morning I thought I'd be asleep.
act1_gather.029: Oh, that's so much worse. You're right. This is better.
act1_gather.030: "I don't know why it's me. But if you want me there, I'll come."
act1_gather.031: …Yeah. Okay. That's a good answer. I was hoping for a funny one, but that's better.
act1_gather.032: Shrug, and look up towards the stairs.
act1_gather.033: Whatever is up there, it has been waiting longer than you have. You can wait with it a little.
act1_gather.034: That's a shrug of acceptance. I'm counting it.
act1_gather.035: The mood in the lobby shifts. Not heavier. Just more careful, the way people get before opening a letter.
act1_gather.036: I'm going first. Obviously. Is there a line? I'm starting the line.
act1_gather.037: You can't start a line with one person.
act1_gather.038: I just did. Look at it. Beautiful line.
act1_gather.039: What if mine is embarrassing, though? Like, what if I sent a video of me singing?
act1_gather.040: It's definitely embarrassing. I believe in you.
act1_gather.041: Records are not embarrassing. They are only old.
act1_gather.042: That's worse! That's so much worse!
act1_gather.044: Hanbi is sitting on the arm of the sofa with his sketchbook closed on his knees. He hasn't said anything since the word *consent*.
act1_gather.045: I think I'd… rather wait. For a bit.
act1_gather.046: Is it alright if I don't decide yet, either? I'm sorry. I'm not sure what's in mine.
act1_gather.048: He says it to the room, but he is looking at Hanbi and Haruta. Then, briefly, at you.
act1_gather.049: Tonight, or ever. That's how I understood it.
act1_gather.050: That is correct. Thank you, Recipient Hamin. You explained it more gently than I did.
act1_gather.051: Right. That's rule one, then. Nobody has to open anything.
act1_gather.052: He writes it down. He actually writes it down, in a small notebook, and underlines it twice.
act1_gather.053: Rule two: we go up together. Nobody sits in a room with a talking building alone.
act1_gather.056: Rule four. If it gets weird in there, I'm allowed to dance until it stops being weird.
act1_gather.057: That's not a rule. That's a threat.
act1_gather.058: It's both. Most good rules are.
act1_gather.059: {{playerName}}. You're really okay with this? Eight rooms. That's… a lot of other people's things.
act1_gather.060: "Only the doors someone wants opened. Only if they want me there."
act1_gather.062: He nods once, slowly, as if he is filing it somewhere safe.
act1_gather.065: At four a.m. I'm going to be asleep on that sofa. Just so everyone knows.
act1_gather.066: Hand him the pencil that's slipped from behind his ear.
act1_gather.068: He tucks it back without finishing the sentence. That seems to be the whole sentence.
act1_gather.069: The Hall of Doors is open. Please go up when you are ready. Or do not. Both are allowed.
act1_gather.070: The stairs creak exactly where they used to. The second floor is a long corridor you don't remember being this long.
act1_gather.071: Eight doors line the hall, four on each side, and every one of them is glowing faintly from the inside, like a paper lantern.
act1_gather.072: On each door, drawn in thin light, a symbol.
act1_gather.073: A wave, cresting. A city skyline at night, its windows lit. A small, round sun.
act1_gather.074: A frame of film. A pair of headphones. A single star.
act1_gather.075: A pencil, mid-line. And at the end, a rainbow, a little lopsided, as if it was drawn in a hurry.
act1_gather.076: That one's mine. The sun. I don't know how I know that. I just do.
act1_gather.077: The rainbow's mine. It's wonky. That's so accurate it's rude.
act1_gather.078: Songha stops in front of the star and doesn't say anything at all, which may be the most surprising thing he has done so far.
act1_gather.079: Eight doors. Eight people standing a careful distance from their own.
act1_gather.080: And you, in the middle of the hall, required.
hub_echo.001: RECIPIENTS PRESENT: 9. RECORDS SEALED: 8. STATUS: TALKING.
hub_echo.002: Please continue. Statistically, it is going well.
hub_echo.003: The founder placed this terminal at the height of a person sitting down. She said people tell the truth sitting down.
hub_echo.004: You are standing. That is also fine.
hub_echo.005: HALL OF DOORS: OPEN. RECORDS RETURNED: 0. RECIPIENTS WAITING: 9.
hub_echo.006: Nobody has opened a door yet. I am not rushing anyone.
hub_echo.007: I have until 05:00. For me, that is a very long time.
hub_echo.008: RECORDS RETURNED: SOME. RECORDS REMAINING: SOME. I am being vague on purpose. It seemed friendlier.
hub_echo.009: Observation: recipients laugh louder after a record is returned. I do not know why.
hub_echo.011: The founder kept a jar of pencils on the front desk. She never bought a single pencil.
hub_echo.012: They simply accumulated. She called this "community."
hub_echo.013: There are forty-one pencils in the jar tonight. One of them is Recipient Hanbi's. He has not noticed yet.
hub_echo.015: It will wait until you are. I am very good at waiting. I have had practice.
hub_echo.016: Observation: it is very quiet now. The rain has stopped. Somebody is snoring on the sofa.
hub_echo.017: I think I like this part of the night best. I did not know I could have a best part.
hamin_intro.001: Hamin is standing by the front desk holding a roll of paper towels he did not have ten minutes ago.
hamin_intro.002: He tears off three squares, folds them once, and sets them on the sofa arm beside Charlie, whose hair is still dripping onto an old flyer.
hamin_intro.003: Oh. Thanks. Wait, where did you even find these?
hamin_intro.005: How do you know there's a staff bathroom?
hamin_intro.008: Justin drifts past behind the sofa, lifts a packet of crackers out of Hyunjun's jacket pocket without breaking stride, and keeps drifting.
hamin_intro.009: He hasn't eaten since lunch. Hyunjun knows. That's why he always buys two.
hamin_intro.010: He says it quietly, to nobody in particular. Then he looks at you, and then, briefly, at the empty can you still haven't found a bin for.
hamin_intro.011: Peach iced tea. In the rain.
hamin_intro.014: You were holding it through your sleeve. It must have been very hot.
hamin_intro.015: Black coffee. At one in the morning.
hamin_intro.016: So you're planning to stay up.
hamin_intro.018: I didn't know anyone actually bought those. I thought they were for decoration.
hamin_intro.019: "Do you always take inventory of people?"
hamin_intro.021: The bin is behind the desk, by the way. Under the lost property box.
hamin_intro.024: The bin is behind the desk. If you were looking for it.
hamin_intro.025: Hand him the can, since he seems to know where it goes.
hamin_intro.026: He takes it without comment and drops it into a bin behind the desk that you would never have found.
hamin_intro.028: There's a heater under the window. It works if you hit the side twice.
hamin_intro.029: I hit it. It's on now. Just so you know.
hamin_intro.030: Did you send something here too? To the Future Letter Project?
hamin_intro.032: I think I sent the sea.
hamin_intro.033: He says it the way other people say *a postcard*.
hamin_intro.034: A recording. From Busan. I was fourteen. It seemed like a good idea at the time.
hamin_intro.036: He remembers exactly why. You can tell by how quickly he looks at the Archive Wall and then away from it.
hamin_intro.037: Also — you were humming. At the door, earlier.
hamin_intro.039: The song from the laundromat. It's been playing the same one on a loop since we got here. Probably since two thousand and ten.
hamin_intro.040: …Sorry. I notice things. I'm not keeping a list.
hamin_intro.041: He is, you suspect, keeping a list.
hamin_intro_repeat.001: The heater's still on. Charlie's mostly dry.
hamin_intro_repeat.002: Justin has eaten one cracker. That's progress.
hamin_intro_repeat.003: He delivers it like a weather report. It is, somehow, the most reassuring thing anyone has said tonight.
hamin_door.001: The second-floor hallway hums. Eight doors, each with light moving behind the frosted glass.
hamin_door.002: Downstairs, Daniel is losing an argument with the claw machine. It sounds like a long argument.
hamin_door.003: Behind Hamin's, the light rises and falls, slowly. Like breathing. Like something coming in and going out.
hamin_door.005: RECORD 02 — OWNER: HAMIN. STATUS: SEALED. AWAITING CONSENT.
hamin_door.006: It's just the sea. Four minutes of it.
hamin_door.007: You might be bored. I'm telling you in advance, so you can't say I didn't warn you.
hamin_door.008: If it's boring, you can leave halfway. I won't notice.
hamin_door.010: He isn't looking at the door. He's looking at the floor in front of it, where the light pools and pulls back.
hamin_door.011: It's fine. You can open it.
hamin_door.012: …That sounded like I was talking to a dentist.
hamin_door.013: What I mean is, I'd like you to be there. If you want to be.
hamin_door.017: He lets out a breath. It isn't quite a laugh.
hamin_door.018: Honestly, that's a relief. I was going to pretend to be calm for another ten minutes.
hamin_door.019: It's waited six years. It can wait a little longer.
hamin_room.002: Not a picture of sand. Sand, or ECHO's best guess at it — cool and fine, giving a little under each step. The hallway is gone behind you.
hamin_room.003: A beach at night. A long curve of dark water, a line of foam that keeps arriving, and far along the shore, the lights of a city that isn't Seoul.
hamin_room.004: RECORD 02 — OWNER: HAMIN. TYPE: VOICE MEMO. LENGTH: FOUR MINUTES, TWELVE SECONDS.
hamin_room.005: LOCATION: A BEACH IN BUSAN. DATE: JULY, SIX YEARS AGO. 23:41.
hamin_room.007: Hamin stands at the edge of it with his hands in his coat pockets, very still, the way people stand at the edge of cold water.
hamin_room.009: I didn't think it would smell right.
hamin_room.010: He looks up the beach, towards the seawall, where a vending machine hums in a square of white light.
hamin_room.012: The vending machine slides one metre to the left, with the faint air of something that has been corrected before and didn't enjoy it.
hamin_room.015: The unresolved subject. That's the part I don't understand.
hamin_room.016: I was alone that night. I'm fairly sure I was alone. I went there specifically to be alone.
hamin_room.019: Everyone's come out of their rooms tonight looking at you with the same face.
hamin_room.020: At this point, it would be stranger if it *wasn't* you.
hamin_room.021: He glances at you. You glance at the sea. Neither of you says the theory out loud.
hamin_room.022: We could not mention it. For a bit. Let it be a surprise.
hamin_room.023: The others came out of their rooms looking at you a bit strangely.
hamin_room.024: I didn't ask. It seemed rude.
hamin_room.026: "If it's me, I apologise in advance."
hamin_room.028: I don't know yet. That's why it's in advance.
hamin_room.030: "Whatever's in here, I'll stay for all four minutes."
hamin_room.033: Stand beside him at the edge and look at the water.
hamin_room.034: He doesn't say anything. After a moment his shoulders come down half an inch, as if he'd been holding them up for both of you.
hamin_room.035: Beginning reconstruction. Please do not step on the owner.
hamin_room.036: The light shifts. The moon moves a few degrees along the sky, as if someone nudged it with one finger.
hamin_room.037: Up the beach, a boy of fourteen sits cross-legged on the sand, holding a phone out towards the water at arm's length. Very seriously.
hamin_room.038: He is trying not to breathe too loudly. You can tell. His whole back is concentrating.
hamin_room.039: Thirty metres further along, there is a shape made of soft light. Knees pulled up. Arms around them. Shivering.
hamin_room.041: The boy looks at the phone. Then at the shape. Then at the phone again, like he's trying to work out which one is his problem.
hamin_room.042: He stops the recording. He stands up. He walks — not to the shape, but past it, up to the vending machine by the seawall.
hamin_room.043: When he comes back, he is holding a can. He holds it out at arm's length, exactly the way he held the phone.
hamin_room.046: It's hot. Corn tea. It was the only hot one.
hamin_room.049: I didn't know the sea got cold at night. We only moved here last week.
hamin_room.050: I thought beaches were a daytime thing.
hamin_room.051: It's a night thing too. Just a different one.

hamin_ending.030: The owner brings two cups on a tray. One is plain barley tea. His. She puts the other one in front of you.
hamin_ending.031: A tall glass of peach iced tea. At six in the morning. In September.
hamin_ending.032: They don't have it in cans. I asked if she could make it. She had peaches. She seemed excited, honestly.
hamin_ending.033: Less ice than normal. You were holding the can by the rim outside, so your fingers wouldn't get cold. So — less ice.
hamin_ending.034: A hot chocolate, steaming just slightly less than hot chocolate usually steams.
hamin_ending.035: I asked for it a bit cooler than normal.
hamin_ending.036: You hold hot things through your sleeve and then wait for them anyway. So I thought — skip the waiting.
hamin_ending.037: A black coffee in a heavy white cup, nothing in it, nothing beside it.
hamin_ending.038: You made a face at the can outside. But you finished it. So I think the face was about the can, not the coffee.
hamin_ending.039: I asked what beans they use. I don't know anything about beans. I nodded a lot.
hamin_ending.040: A can of grape soda, sweating a little, standing very upright in the middle of a café that does not sell anything in cans.
hamin_ending.041: They didn't have it. There's a convenience store on the corner.
hamin_ending.042: I asked if I could bring it in. She said it was the strangest thing anyone had asked her all week. I think it was a compliment.
hamin_ending.044: While you were taking your coat off.
hamin_ending.045: I said "next time". Six years ago. I don't say a lot of things. So I try to keep the ones I do.
hamin_ending.046: The sun gets the rest of the way through the window, lands on the table, and stays there, as if it's been told this is the place.
hamin_ending.047: He is watching you take the first sip. Not the drink. You. Checking it's right, the way he's checked everything all night.
hamin_ending.049: It's not a big deal, but—
hamin_ending.050: This place opens at five-thirty. Every day.
hamin_ending.052: "Tomorrow, then. And the day after that."
hamin_ending.053: …You don't have to decide the day after that right now.
hamin_ending.055: You keep doing that. Deciding things out loud before I've finished being nervous about them.
hamin_ending.056: "Are you asking me to breakfast, or reading me the opening hours?"
hamin_ending.058: …Breakfast. I'm asking you to breakfast. Songha would be proud of how long it took me to say that.
hamin_ending.059: "I unpacked the kettle last week. I think that means I'm staying."
hamin_ending.061: It's always the last thing. If the kettle's out, I'm not leaving.
hamin_ending.062: …Then I'll stop checking the exits for you.
hamin_ending.063: You have always left. New city, new school, a season and then the boxes again. You always left in spring.
hamin_ending.064: It is September. Spring is a long way off. And for the first time, you aren't counting towards it.
hamin_ending.065: On the table, his hand has ended up next to yours. Not on it. Next to it. Close enough that it's a question.
hamin_ending.066: You answer it. His fingers are still a little cold from the walk over. That's fine. You have a hot drink, or a cold one, and all morning.
hamin_ending.070: He slides the sugar over to you without being asked, even though you don't take any. Then he realises, and slides it back, and hides his face in his cup.
hamin_ending.073: …Good. I'll get the next one. Same thing?

daniel_route.102: Let your shoulder rest against his.

daniel_route.104: Turn your hand palm-up on the floor between you.

daniel_route.111: I made the list because I thought—
daniel_route.112: If it went quiet, you'd notice there wasn't anything else. No arcade. No games. Just me, in a room.
daniel_route.113: And that's not— it's not much.

daniel_route.123: Is this okay? This. Just this?

daniel_route.127: …What do you do? When it's quiet. Wherever you live now.

daniel_route.132: Okay. Good. I mean— not good. Fair. It's fair.
daniel_route.135: It ticks. It's a good listener.
daniel_route.136: I'm going to be a good listener. Watch. Starting now.
daniel_route.141: He says it like a fact he's just checked, and found to be true.
daniel_route.143: I have one strip of film left in the reconstruction. Four frames. I would like to use it, if you would like to be in it.
daniel_route.145: Only the rain. It is in the record. I cannot take it out.
daniel_route.146: That's okay. The rain can stay.
daniel_route.147: The booth builds itself around the two of you out of soft light. The bench. The curtain. The little screen.
daniel_route.148: The rain on the roof. The same rain, applauding nobody.

daniel_route.150: The screen lights up. FOUR FRAMES. SMILE!

daniel_route.152: FRAME ONE. His hand comes up — peace sign, tongue half out — and stops halfway, like he's just remembered he doesn't have to.
daniel_route.153: He laughs at himself, and puts the hand down.
daniel_route.154: Pull a face at the camera.
daniel_route.155: FRAME TWO. You, making the worst face of your life on purpose. Daniel, staring at you, delighted and betrayed. That was supposed to be his job.
daniel_route.156: Look at him instead of the camera.
daniel_route.157: FRAME TWO. The camera catches you looking at him. It catches him catching you. Neither of you looks away in time.
daniel_route.158: Sit still and let it happen.
daniel_route.159: FRAME TWO. Two people on a bench. One of them is trying very hard not to grin, and losing.
daniel_route.160: FRAME THREE. Both of you laughing at nothing in particular, which is the best thing there is to laugh at.
daniel_route.161: The screen counts down to the last frame. Five. Four.
daniel_route.164: He turns towards you. Slowly, so you can see it coming. So you could say no.
daniel_route.167: He leans in until his forehead rests against yours. His hair is soft and ridiculous and smells faintly of the arcade.
daniel_route.168: Your hand is still in his. It has been, the whole time.

daniel_route.171: He leans back against the booth wall. After a second, his shoulder settles against yours, and stays.
daniel_route.172: He doesn't look at the camera. He looks at the curtain, and the rain, and — once, quickly, like he's checking you're still there — at you.
daniel_route.175: Nobody posing. Nobody performing. Two people on a bench, waiting out a rain that is only a memory, in no hurry at all for it to stop.
daniel_route.176: The booth prints the strip with a whirr and a small, satisfied click.
daniel_route.177: RECORD 08. FRAMES FIVE THROUGH EIGHT: APPENDED. CONDITION: DRY.
daniel_route.178: I have never added to a record before. I believe it was allowed.
daniel_route.179: Daniel holds the new strip up by one corner, like it might still be wet.
daniel_route.180: Frame one: me, quitting halfway. That's growth. Write that down.
daniel_route.181: Frame three: we look insane. Good. Correct.
daniel_route.182: And look at the last one.
daniel_route.183: That's my favourite. Again. Two for two.
daniel_route.184: The booth dims around you until it is only the room again. The radiator. The stripe of light under the door.

daniel_route.189: We got to it early. Kind of. I skipped five whole things.
daniel_route.190: Songha's going to look at this page and think I got kidnapped.
daniel_route.191: Tell him number eleven took longer than planned.
daniel_route.193: I don't want to plan anything else tonight. I just want—
daniel_route.194: Can I just want this? Is that allowed?
daniel_route.196: He lets out a breath that sounds like it has been waiting two years.
daniel_route.197: I think I'm getting better at it. Nothing. Sitting.
daniel_route.199: Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
daniel_route.200: All recipients: please come to the lobby. It is almost time. I would like everyone to be there.
daniel_route.202: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and doesn't let go of it on the stairs. Not once.
daniel_route.203: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and lets go a second later than he needs to.
daniel_ending.001: The Archive Wall is almost dark now. Hundreds of little glass boxes, gone quiet one by one. Only the eighth is still lit.
daniel_ending.003: Writing four frames. Then four more. Then a note in the margin: "Condition: dry."
daniel_ending.004: A small glass card slides out of a slot in the front desk that you never knew was there. It is warm, like a cup someone has just put down.
daniel_ending.005: Inside the glass: eight tiny frames. A pose. A startle. Two strangers laughing. Two strangers sitting.
daniel_ending.006: Then the new four, all the way down to the last one, where nobody is doing anything at all.
daniel_ending.007: …It's so small. Why is it so small? I thought it'd be, like, a poster.
daniel_ending.008: Is that the booth one? Let me see— oh. *Oh*. Frame eight. Hyung.
daniel_ending.009: Of course it's the booth one. I would've put money on it. I did, actually. Hyunjun owes me three thousand won.
daniel_ending.010: I said the claw machine! That's basically the same thing! It's the same *genre*!
daniel_ending.011: Frame one's great, by the way. That's a professional pose. I respect it.
daniel_ending.012: The last frame is good. Nobody would have written it like that. That's why it works.
daniel_ending.015: Daniel doesn't say anything. He holds the card up to the last light of the Archive Wall and grins at it like it just told him a secret.
daniel_ending.016: Then he turns the card round so you can see it too, and keeps it there, between the two of you, where both of you can hold an edge.
daniel_ending.017: ECHO? Thanks. For keeping it. Even wet.
daniel_ending.018: You are welcome, Recipient Daniel. It was my favourite record to be bad at.
daniel_ending.019: Also, I'd like my notebook back.
daniel_ending.020: You'll get it back! I only used one page. And a half. There's a drawing of Mr. Kim.
daniel_ending.021: Hongdae at twenty to six is a different city. Shutters down. A street sweeper humming. Two pigeons holding a meeting about a dropped triangle kimbap.
daniel_ending.022: It's a fifteen-minute walk from Studio 25 to here. Daniel made it take forty.
daniel_ending.023: He stopped at every photo booth on the way and looked inside, like he was checking on old friends.
daniel_ending.024: The others went ahead to breakfast. Hamin said he'd order for everyone. Songha said he'd order for Hamin.
daniel_ending.025: The arcade is closed. The booth outside it is a newer one — pink, with a sticker promising the best photos in Mapo.
daniel_ending.026: The awning is exactly as useless as you remember.
daniel_ending.027: You and Daniel are sitting on the step beside it. Nobody decided to. It just happened, about twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.028: Mr. Kim's former prisoner sits on the step between you, watching the sky go from grey to peach.
daniel_ending.029: His phone buzzes. He reads it. He doesn't answer it.
daniel_ending.031: He stands, and stretches until something in his back clicks, and pats his pockets for nothing in particular.
daniel_ending.034: You said that twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.036: He looks at you. Then at the street. Then he sits back down.
daniel_ending.038: You have never once in your life asked for five more minutes.
daniel_ending.039: You were always the one who knew exactly when to leave. The thank-you over the shoulder. The curtain swinging shut behind you. The rain stopping, and you going with it.
daniel_ending.040: Daniel's head comes to rest on your shoulder, heavy and warm, and his hand finds yours on the step as if it has done it a hundred times.
daniel_ending.043: Okay. Just checking. I'm going to keep checking. Forever, probably.
daniel_ending.044: Daniel's shoulder settles against yours. His knee doesn't bounce once.
daniel_ending.047: I'm not going to say anything else. Look at me. Not saying anything else.
daniel_ending.048: He doesn't fill the silence. He doesn't need to.
daniel_ending.049: The street does it for him: a shutter going up, a bike bell, a pigeon with opinions. The light coming up over Mapo like it has nowhere else to be.
daniel_ending.052: Not the ECHO kind. The normal kind.
daniel_ending.053: This counts. This is my favourite frame.
daniel_ending.054: There's no camera. He doesn't seem to mind.
daniel_newmem.001: A week later. A Tuesday, which is the least eventful day ever invented.
daniel_newmem.002: Hongdae, three in the afternoon. The pink booth by the arcade has a queue of exactly one person, and he is waving at you with both arms.
daniel_newmem.003: {{playerName}}! You came! I wasn't sure you'd— no, I was sure. I was mostly sure.
daniel_newmem.004: Okay. So. ECHO's asleep. The Future Letter Project is closed. The studio is currently full of men with drills.
daniel_newmem.005: Which means somebody has to keep the archive going. Unofficially. Me. I'm the archive now.
daniel_newmem.007: One strip. Four frames. Every week, until I run out of money, which will be soon.
daniel_newmem.008: Songha made me a spreadsheet for it. Hanbi bought me a folder. Charlie keeps asking what the folder's for.
daniel_newmem.009: The booth is exactly as narrow as the other one. Some things are just standard.
daniel_newmem.010: Frame one, pose. Frame two, pose worse. Frame three, whatever happens happens.
daniel_newmem.014: Frame one: a peace sign, and a worse peace sign.
daniel_newmem.015: Frame two: a face you will deny making.
daniel_newmem.016: Frame three: whatever happened. It's mostly elbows.
daniel_newmem.017: Frame four: two people on a bench, not doing anything, for almost the whole three seconds.
daniel_newmem.018: Then, at the very last instant, Daniel's composure breaks, and the camera catches him laughing at absolutely nothing.
daniel_newmem.019: That still counts! Nobody said nothing had to be *quiet*.
daniel_newmem.020: The machine prints two copies, still warm. He hands you one without looking at it, like it was always going to be yours.
daniel_newmem.022: I was going to say that! That's my whole line. You keep taking my lines.
daniel_newmem.023: Tuck the strip into your coat. The inside pocket, where the rain can't get it.
daniel_newmem.024: …Good. Good pocket choice. Very dry. I approve.
daniel_newmem.026: Daniel looks at the sky, then at the booth, then at you.

interlude_2.001: Four doors now. The lobby has become a kind of camp: shoes by the sofa, jackets on the backs of chairs, somebody's socks drying on the radiator.

interlude_3.031: Two left. Nobody breathe. Hyunjun, this is your "one more."
interlude_3.033: Okay! Timer's on! Ten seconds! Nine! Nobody blink! Eight! Why is Charlie—
interlude_3.034: Wait, what's happening? Are we doing the nice one or the silly one?
interlude_3.036: The picture slides out of the camera, grey and blank. Nine people crowd around a square of nothing, waiting.
interlude_3.037: Slowly, it develops: a blur of arms and hair and the corner of the front desk. Justin mid-fall. Hyunjun too high. Hanbi's hand on somebody's shoulder.
interlude_3.038: And you, right in it. Not at the edge. Laughing at something you can't remember now, and will not forget.
interlude_3.039: Afterwards, the lobby goes soft. People settle in twos, the way people do at three in the morning.
interlude_3.040: By the window, Hanbi and Songha are sharing one earbud each and pretending not to be tired.
interlude_3.041: I didn't plan any of this.
interlude_3.042: I know. It's been nice watching.
interlude_3.043: On the sofa, Justin gives Hyunjun the last of the shrimp crackers. Hyunjun stares at the bag like it might be a trick.
interlude_3.045: Don't make it weird. It's a limited-time offer.
interlude_3.046: Charlie has fallen asleep sitting up, his head sliding slowly onto Daniel's shoulder. Daniel, for once in his life, is holding perfectly still.
interlude_3.047: {{playerName}}. Don't make me laugh. If I laugh, he wakes up.
interlude_3.048: And if he wakes up, he's going to ask what's happening. And I don't know. I genuinely don't know any more.
interlude_3.049: He says it in a whisper, and he is smiling, and he doesn't move a single muscle.
interlude_3.050: Hamin and Haruta are side by side at the front desk, watching the photo finish developing as if it's a film that might still change its ending.
interlude_3.056: The whole room hears it. Charlie wakes up. Nobody says anything.
interlude_3.057: Not now, if you don't want. Whenever you want.
interlude_3.058: Nobody has to open anything. That goes for you too.
interlude_3.060: Soon's good. Soon's a real time. I can write that down.
interlude_3.061: "After the other doors. I'm saving the weird one for last."
interlude_3.063: Look at the photo in Hamin's hands instead.
interlude_3.064: Nine people in a square of expired film. That, at least, is a record you already know how to read.
interlude_3.065: Wait. Who gets to keep the photo? There's only one. Plus the nostril one.
interlude_3.066: I'll make a rotation. A week each, alphabetical—
interlude_3.068: …Okay. Later. We'll figure it out later.
act3_start.001: Eight doors, all of them dark now. Eight records returned. The Hall of Doors should be finished.
act3_start.002: It isn't. At the end of the corridor, where there was only wall an hour ago, there is a ninth door.
act3_start.003: It has no symbol. Just a small brass plate, the kind that used to be on the front desk, and on it a name.
act3_start.005: RECORD 09 — OWNER: {{playerName}}. TYPE: LETTER. DATE: SIX YEARS AGO. STATUS: SEALED.
act3_start.006: I did not know this record existed until 00:25. It was filed under FRONT DESK — MISC. I apologise. My filing was not always good.
act3_start.007: A letter. You wrote a Future Letter. While you worked here.
act3_start.010: It's true. You remember the desk, the forms, the pencils. You don't remember sitting down and writing one yourself.
act3_start.011: …Okay. That's allowed. It was six years ago.
act3_start.012: "Everyone who worked here had to. It was in the contract."
act3_start.014: There wasn't. There was a founder who said "you too" and pushed a form across the desk. Same thing.
act3_start.015: Look at the brass plate and say nothing.
act3_start.016: The name is in your own handwriting. Younger. Rounder. Somebody who pressed too hard with the pencil.
act3_start.017: It's the same rule. Nobody has to open anything.
act3_start.019: The owner's consent is required. I will wait. I have been waiting six years. A few more minutes will not register.
act3_start.022: That's fine. We're not going anywhere.
act3_start.023: Yeah! We'll just — stand here. In a hallway. At three-thirty in the morning. Like normal people.
act3_start.024: They do, too. Nobody checks the time. Nobody says "we've only got until five." Eight people lean on a wall and wait for you.
act3_start.025: Hyunjun starts humming something. Justin taps the beat on the radiator. It is, absurdly, comfortable.
act3_start.026: After a while, the door doesn't seem so heavy.
act3_room.001: The front desk of Studio 25, six years ago. Rain on the window. A radio somewhere playing a song that was already old.
act3_room.002: ECHO has rebuilt it from the inside out: the sign-up forms, the jar of pencils, the corkboard. A stack of moving boxes by the wall, half-taped, with a city name on each one.
act3_room.003: Busan. Seoul. Seoul again. A city abroad, the name in a different alphabet. Seoul.
act3_room.004: And at the desk, a figure of soft light. Sixteen. Sleeves too long. Writing something with a pencil pressed far too hard.
act3_room.005: The boxes have *labels*. That's so many cities.
act3_room.008: It's a strange thing to say out loud in a room made of your own past. The boxes make it look like a fact instead of a feeling.
act3_room.009: That's… that's a lot of last days.
act3_room.011: Okay, but were you good at *unpacking*?
act3_room.012: You look at the boxes. Half-taped. You don't answer, and he's kind enough to let it go.
act3_room.014: Hamin glances at the boxes, then at you, and doesn't ask anything. He just moves a little closer to where you're standing.
act3_room.016: The figure at the desk finishes writing. Folds the paper twice. Slides it into the slot — the one that sticks — and has to push it with two fingers.
act3_room.017: You too, kid. Everybody who works here writes one. Studio rules.
act3_room.018: The founder, off to one side, sleeves rolled up, laughing at something on her phone. Seo Yeonhwa. You had forgotten her voice. You had not forgotten her laugh.
act3_room.019: What if I'm not here to read it?
act3_room.020: Then it'll wait. That's what the building's for.
act3_room.021: The letter unfolds in the air in front of you, the way ECHO unfolds everything — too carefully, like it's afraid of tearing.
act3_room.022: You know the handwriting. You don't know the words until you read them.
act3_room.023: "Dear future me. I don't know where you are when you read this. I don't know what city. I've stopped guessing."
act3_room.024: "I hope you're okay. I hope you found people. I hope you stayed long enough that somebody learned how you take your drink."
act3_room.025: "I hope, by the time you read this, you've found a place you want to stay."
act3_room.026: Hanbi is the first to speak, and it isn't with words. He takes a breath in, holds it, lets it go.
act3_room.027: …That's a lot to ask of a letter.
act3_room.028: It's not asking the letter. It's asking you.
act3_room.030: It comes out steadier than you expected. Nobody rushes to fill the silence after it.
act3_room.032: Two words. He means tonight. He might mean more than tonight. He doesn't explain, and you don't ask him to.
act3_room.034: It's *so* covered. Half this building knows your order now.
act3_room.035: Hamin looks at the floor with the specific expression of somebody who has been caught remembering something.
act3_room.036: Fold the letter back up and hold it.
act3_room.037: The paper is warm, the way ECHO's things are warm. Daniel looks like he wants to say a joke and decides, visibly, not to.
act3_room.038: You don't have to answer it tonight. It's a letter. It's patient.
act3_link.002: RECORD 01 through 08 each contain one unresolved subject. RECORD 09 resolves them.
act3_link.004: The front desk folds away. In its place, a room made of other rooms.
act3_link.005: A beach at night. The last train. An airport board. A cinema seat. A doorway with a key ring on the hook. A rooftop. A lounge sofa. A photo booth.
act3_link.006: Eight rooms, stitched together at the edges like a quilt. And in every one of them, standing where the silhouette stood: a younger version of you, in a coat with sleeves too long.
act3_link.007: Subject: {{playerName}}. Appears in eight records over six years, in four cities.
act3_link.008: Encounters were brief. None exceeded one night. None were repeated. The subject was, on each occasion, about to leave.
act3_link.010: I searched for one. For some time. There is no pattern. There is no signal. There is no schedule. I am sorry if that is disappointing.
act3_link.011: No pattern. Eight times. That's — statistically, that's —
act3_link.012: It's fate. Right? That's what this is. It has to be. Nine people, one building, the same night —
act3_link.013: It's not fate. ECHO just said. It looked.
act3_link.014: ECHO's a *filing system*, hyung. It wouldn't know fate if fate walked in and asked for the wifi password.
act3_link.017: Whether it was fate. Does it change what happened?
act3_link.019: It surprises you as you say it, and then it doesn't. If it were fate, none of it would have been anyone's choice.
act3_link.020: A kid who gave a stranger a hot can on a beach. A kid who stayed on a train. A kid who said "you don't have to stop."
act3_link.021: Those were chosen. Every one of them.
act3_link.023: I'd rather have chosen it too.
act3_link.024: "If it's fate, fate has terrible timing. Six years?"
act3_link.025: Fate showed up eight times and forgot to introduce itself. Fate's a mess.
act3_link.026: To be fair. So were we. I didn't even get a name.
act3_link.027: Hyunjun says it lightly. It isn't light. Nobody pretends it is.
act3_link.029: That's the whole film, I think. Someone was there. Someone noticed. That's — that's the whole film.
act3_link.030: No plot twist. Just people. I can work with that.
act3_link.031: Songha looks at his notebook for a long moment. Then he closes it.
act3_link.032: Okay. No pattern. I'm writing down "no pattern" and I'm going to let that be an answer.
act3_link.033: Look at him. Growth. At three-forty in the morning.
act3_founder.001: One more item is attached to RECORD 09. It is not the owner's. It is the founder's. She asked that it be played "to whoever's left at the end."
act3_founder.002: You are whoever is left. Playing.
act3_founder.003: Hello. If you're hearing this, it's the last night, and ECHO's being dramatic about it. Ignore that. It gets like this.
act3_founder.004: I built this place because people kept saying "someday." Someday I'll record that song. Someday I'll tell them. Someday I'll go back.
act3_founder.005: So I gave someday a mailbox. That's all the Future Letter Project ever was. A mailbox for later.
act3_founder.006: But here's the thing I figured out too late, kids, and I want you to have it now, for free:
act3_founder.007: Archives are for keeping. People aren't.
act3_founder.008: Don't keep each other. Meet each other. Again. On purpose. That's the trick. Okay. That's the message. Somebody turn the lights off when you go.
act3_founder.010: That's the best advice I've ever gotten from a wall.
act3_founder.011: It is 03:50. Time remaining: seventy minutes.
act3_founder.012: The building is yours until then. I have no further records. I have no further rules.
act3_founder.013: Recipient {{playerName}} — you have been in eight of our memories tonight. Where would you like to be, for the ninth?
act3_choice.001: The lobby again. Everyone drifts apart the way people do at the end of a long night, not leaving — just spreading out into the building.
act3_choice.002: Somebody goes up to the roof. Somebody goes to the practice room. Somebody sits on the worst sofa in Seoul.
act3_choice.003: Seventy minutes. One building. Where do you want to be?
act4_choice.001: 04:57. Everyone is back in the lobby without anyone having called them. The building did it, somehow — or the hour did.
act4_choice.002: The Archive Wall is dark except for a soft line of light running along the front desk, like a shoreline.
act4_choice.003: It is 04:57. My power will be cut in three minutes.
act4_choice.004: I can write one record to the keepsake card. One. The card is small. I requested a larger card. Nobody replied.
act4_choice.005: Recipient {{playerName}} — you are the subject every record shares. The choice is yours. Please choose one record to preserve.
act4_choice.007: So much pressure. Historic amounts of pressure. Take your time. You have three minutes.
echo_farewell.002: Nine recipients present. Zero records unclaimed. That has never happened before.
echo_farewell.003: I was built to keep things until someone came back for them. Tonight everyone came back. I find that I do not know what to do with my hands. I do not have hands. The feeling persists.
echo_farewell.004: Thank you for opening the doors. Thank you for saying "not yet" when you needed to. I have logged those too. They were also records.
echo_farewell.005: Goodnight. Please turn off the lights when you go. She asked.
echo_farewell.006: The line of light along the desk goes out. Then the glow in the walls. Then the low hum under everything that you had stopped hearing hours ago.
echo_farewell.007: For a moment the lobby is completely dark and completely quiet, and nine people breathe in it.
echo_farewell.008: A phone torch clicks on. Hanbi's, of course.
echo_farewell.010: Was that — did the building just say goodnight? I'm never going to be normal about this.
echo_farewell.011: You were never normal about anything. That's your whole thing.
echo_farewell.012: Somewhere outside, the laundromat's sign buzzes back on. The sky in the window has gone from black to the deep blue of a bruise healing.
true_ending.001: It comes out before you've decided to say it. The way true things do.
true_ending.004: "You don't have to keep any of it. We'll keep each other."
true_ending.005: "Delete the lot. We're going to breakfast."
true_ending.007: Eight people look at you. Then at each other. Then — slowly, like a wave deciding — they start to nod.
true_ending.009: Yeah! Yes. One more of *everything*. Starting now.
true_ending.010: Step one: breakfast. I'll allow it. I'll allow it without a schedule.
true_ending.011: Wait, are we really not keeping anything? Not even the photo?
true_ending.012: We have the photo. It's in your pocket, Charlie. It's a photo.
true_ending.013: …Oh. Right. Right! We have the photo.
true_ending.014: Then it isn't an ending. It's a cut to the next scene.
true_ending.015: And the next scene has eggs in it.
true_ending.017: Recipient {{playerName}}. Nine recipients. Zero records selected for preservation.
true_ending.018: I have checked the request three times. It is consistent. Then there is nothing I need to keep.
true_ending.019: I understand now what she meant. It took me six years and one night. I was not built quickly.
true_ending.020: Meet each other again. On purpose. I will not be here to see it. That is correct. That is how it should work.
true_ending.021: Goodnight, everyone. Thank you for the new memory. I am not keeping it. I am just — holding it a moment.
true_ending.022: The lights go. The hum goes. The building becomes a building.
true_ending.023: In the dark, someone — Hyunjun, it's definitely Hyunjun — says "one more minute," and everyone laughs, and nobody moves.
true_dawn.001: Sunrise on the alley behind the laundromat. Peach light on wet brick. The STUDIO 25 sign with its crooked 2, going gold for the first and last time.
true_dawn.002: Nine people on the step, blinking at the sky like it's a rumour that turned out to be true.
true_dawn.003: The only place open at 06:40 is a kimbap shop with three tables. Nine people fit at three tables if two of them stand and Charlie sits on a crate.
true_dawn.004: Songha orders for everyone without asking, then asks everyone, then re-orders. Hanbi pays before anyone notices. Daniel notices and yells about it.
true_dawn.005: Hyung, you can't just *pay*. That's a hostile act. We were going to split it.
true_dawn.007: Okay, real question, no jokes. Same time next week?
true_dawn.008: Next week is fine. I'm writing it down. I'm not writing anything *else* down. Just the day.
true_dawn.011: Can we go somewhere with more chairs next time? Not for me. For the crate. The crate deserves rest.
true_dawn.012: I know a cinema with chairs. Terrible chairs. But a lot of them.
true_dawn.013: Sold. I'm sold. Movie night. What are we watching?
true_dawn.015: He says it like he's testing whether the sentence holds weight. It does. Everyone hears it hold.
true_dawn.016: Hamin slides a cup across the table toward you without looking up. It is, of course, exactly right.
true_dawn.017: Less ice. They put too much.
true_dawn.018: I asked them to cool it a bit. You burn your tongue.
true_dawn.020: They had grape. Don't ask how.
true_dawn.021: "You're going to have to stop doing that. It's unsettling."
true_dawn.025: It is. He knows it is. He drinks his own coffee to avoid saying so.
true_dawn.026: Take the cup and clink it gently against his.
true_dawn.028: Okay. Okay okay okay. Everyone. Phones out. Not a photo — I've had enough photos — just, everybody put next week in.
true_dawn.031: Eight phones come out around three tables in a kimbap shop at ten to seven in the morning. Nobody's going anywhere. Nobody's leaving in spring.
true_dawn.032: Outside the window, the city wakes up without any idea what it missed.
true_dawn.033: You stayed until morning. Turns out that's the trick. You just keep doing it.
true_dawn.034: Later, someone will ask how you all met. It's going to take a while to explain.
true_dawn.035: "It's a long story," you'll say. "It's a good one."
friendship_route.001: *Stay with everyone.* It comes out simpler than you expected.
friendship_route.002: Like it was the answer the whole time, and just needed saying in a room with people in it.
friendship_route.003: Correct answer. Ding ding ding. No notes.
friendship_route.004: Everyone! We get everyone! That's the best answer! That's the most answer!
friendship_route.006: He has the notebook out. Seven people groan in perfect unison.
friendship_route.008: Everyone is already moving towards the stairs.
friendship_route.009: Why does everyone listen to him and not me?
friendship_route.010: I don't say much. So it counts more.
friendship_route.011: That's so unfair. That's so unfair and so correct.
friendship_route.012: Justin and I will do one more store run. One more! The last one! We'll meet you up there!
friendship_route.013: I'm going to steal everything he buys. For balance.
friendship_route.014: On the way up, you pass the Hall of Doors. It's dim now. Eight doors stand open, their symbols gone soft and grey, like chalk after rain.
friendship_route.015: At the end of the corridor, where there used to be only wall, a ninth door stands open too.
friendship_route.016: It's weird. Like a practice room after everyone's gone home.
friendship_route.017: It's nice, though. Everything that was in there… it's out here now.
friendship_route.018: The rooftop door sticks, and then gives, and then the whole sky is there.
friendship_route.019: The rain has washed Mapo clean. The streets below are wet and orange. Above them, the kind of stars Seoul almost never lets you see.
friendship_route.020: Someone drags up the blankets from the lobby. Someone else brings the cushions from Charlie's fort, which he insists on rebuilding at once.
friendship_route.021: Fort two. Rooftop edition. Now with sky.
friendship_route.022: Twelve minutes later, Hyunjun and Justin come through the door with two bags each, out of breath.
friendship_route.023: They are arguing about whether shrimp crackers are "a snack" or "a lifestyle."
friendship_route.024: Right behind them, there is a knock on the rooftop door, and a delivery rider in a helmet holding a warm, heavy bag.
friendship_route.025: Tteokbokki. From the twenty-four-hour place in Hapjeong. I ordered at 03:51.
friendship_route.027: It's been a long night. I've been learning. I cut every step except the one that mattered.
friendship_route.028: Tteokbokki *and* convenience store! Both! Both is a food group! I said this hours ago!
friendship_route.029: It becomes a feast on a blanket: rice cakes too hot to eat, ramen going soft, kimbap, chips, a bag of tangerines nobody remembers buying.
friendship_route.030: {{playerName}}. I got you something. Don't make it a thing.
friendship_route.031: A triangle kimbap. Tuna mayo. The correct answer, he told you hours ago, when you picked one out of his bag. He remembered.
friendship_route.032: A carton of banana milk, straw already stuck to the side. The one you rescued from Justin, hours ago. He remembered.
friendship_route.033: An ice cream bar, a little soft from the run up the stairs. Rain or not, hours ago, that was your pick. He remembered.
friendship_route.034: A little of everything, all in a pile, as if he couldn't decide and refused to have to.
friendship_route.035: It's a thing. I know. I made it a thing.
friendship_route.036: Hamin sits down next to you and slides a can along the blanket until it touches your hand. He doesn't comment on it. He doesn't need to.
friendship_route.037: Can I have the corner piece of tteokbokki? The burnt one. I want it. I'm saying that out loud.
friendship_route.038: Haruta wants something! Everybody, silence! Give the man the burnt one!
friendship_route.040: Recipients. May I ask what this activity is called?
friendship_route.044: Noted. I have created a new category.
friendship_route.045: Okay. Game. Because I physically cannot help it.
friendship_route.046: "Most likely to." I say a thing, everyone points at who it is. No arguing. Only pointing.
friendship_route.047: Most likely to still be awake at five a.m.
friendship_route.048: Eight fingers point at Daniel. Daniel points at the rooftop speaker.
friendship_route.049: ECHO. Obviously. It's literally its job.
friendship_route.050: Until 05:00. Then I will be asleep. I will not be pointing at anyone.
friendship_route.051: Most likely to cry at the group photo.
friendship_route.052: Everyone points at Hyunjun. Hyunjun, after a moment of dignified consideration, points at himself.
friendship_route.053: That's fair. That's completely fair. I'm going to cry at it tomorrow as well.
friendship_route.054: Most likely to make a schedule for the group chat.
friendship_route.055: I don't need you to point. I know.
friendship_route.056: Everyone points anyway. Songha points at himself too, a little proudly.
friendship_route.057: Most likely to fall asleep before the game's over.
friendship_route.058: Nobody needs to point. Charlie is already asleep, curled inside Fort Two, holding a tangerine.
friendship_route.060: He stops. It's too close to something. The rooftop goes quiet for half a second, and everyone is very carefully not looking at you.
friendship_route.061: No. Scratch that. New one. Most likely to *come back*.
friendship_route.062: Eight fingers, one after the other, point at you.
friendship_route.064: It feels like signing something. It feels like a promise that you want to keep.
friendship_route.065: Unanimous! First unanimous vote of the night!
friendship_route.066: Point at Daniel. "You're coming back for the claw machine."
friendship_route.067: …I *am* coming back for the claw machine. That's an accurate point. I respect it.
friendship_route.069: Then I'll come back for the new claw machine.
friendship_route.070: Point at all of them, one by one.
friendship_route.071: It takes a while. Nobody interrupts. When you reach the last one, Hanbi is smiling at his shoes.
friendship_route.072: After the food, the rooftop goes horizontal. Nine people lying on blankets, looking up, trading half-sentences with the sky.
friendship_route.073: Charlie falls asleep for eleven minutes and wakes up in the middle of an argument about which constellation is shaped like a ladle.
friendship_route.074: You get up to stretch. Somehow that turns into going round the roof, one person at a time.
friendship_route.078: He lifts one side of his coat, and waits. Not assuming. Just offering.
friendship_route.079: You nod. He puts it round your shoulders and goes back to looking at the sky like nothing happened.
friendship_route.080: I didn't use to ask. I just used to move people out of the wind. I'm trying to ask now.
friendship_route.081: I've decided something. I'm staying up here until the power goes. Not because everyone is.
friendship_route.082: Because I want to. That's the whole reason. It's strange how good that feels to say.
friendship_route.084: I want to. There. Twice in one night. Somebody should write it down.
friendship_route.085: Justin is sitting on the ledge-side bench, not dancing. His fingers tap on his knee: five, six, seven, eight.
friendship_route.086: I'm not doing a bit, by the way. Right now. This is just me.
friendship_route.087: It's quieter than I thought. Being just me. It's… okay, actually.
friendship_route.089: Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
friendship_route.090: Songha has put the notebook face down on the blanket. He points up at a star, very confidently.
friendship_route.093: It is tonight. I've decided. No plan, no research. Just Gerald.
friendship_route.095: No idea. I'll look it up. Later. Not tonight.
friendship_route.096: Hanbi turns his sketchbook round. Nine tiny figures on a rooftop. One of them is holding a can. One of them is pointing at a star named Gerald.
friendship_route.097: It's rough. I'll fix the hands later.
friendship_route.098: I'm glad you came tonight. {p}That's all. I wanted to say it out loud.
friendship_route.099: I hate this part. The part where you can see the end coming.
friendship_route.100: But it's still happening. Right now. And after it's over, it'll still have happened. That's… that's something, right?
friendship_route.102: Okay. Yeah. I'm writing that on my hand.
friendship_route.103: Where are you going after this?
friendship_route.104: Home. I think. Wherever that is this month.
friendship_route.105: Wherever the snacks are. That's the rule. You made that one up, you know. Years ago.
friendship_route.106: There are so many snacks up here. So technically you're home.
friendship_route.107: Daniel is lying flat on his back with his arms spread out, doing nothing at all.
friendship_route.108: I haven't planned anything for the next ten minutes. No game. Nothing.
friendship_route.109: It's terrifying. It's fine. It's actually really fine.
friendship_route.110: You lie down next to him. Neither of you says anything for a while. He doesn't fill it.
friendship_route.114: The sky goes from black to the deep blue that comes just before the deep blue that comes before morning.
friendship_route.115: Across the rooftops, one window lights up. Someone else in Mapo is awake, making coffee, starting a day. It feels like being waved at.
friendship_route.116: Justin and Hyunjun are sharing the last bag of shrimp crackers. Nobody is stealing. It is, as Hyunjun says, historic.
friendship_route.117: What's everyone doing tomorrow? Honestly. Not the schedule.
friendship_route.118: Sleeping until two. Then eating. Then sleeping.
friendship_route.119: Then it's your turn. You have moved house more times than you can count on both hands. You know exactly what you usually say next.
friendship_route.120: "I think I'm going to stay. In this city. For a while."
friendship_route.121: It's the first time you've said it out loud. It sounds truer outside your head than it did in it.
friendship_route.122: Then I'm adding you to the schedule. Permanently. You can't unsubscribe.
friendship_route.123: "Unpacking. There are boxes in my room I've been ignoring for a month."
friendship_route.124: We'll help. Nine people can unpack anything. We'll make it a game.
friendship_route.125: He will actually make it a game.
friendship_route.126: …Then I guess I'm staying long enough to unpack.
friendship_route.127: "Maybe I'll stay." Say it quietly. Only the sky has to hear.
friendship_route.128: It isn't only the sky. Hamin hears it. You can tell because he doesn't turn his head, and because he smiles.
friendship_route.130: Please come down to the lobby. I have one question. And then I have to go.
friendship_route.132: We'll come back up. After. Come on.
friendship_route.133: Nine people fold up the blankets badly and go down the stairs together, slower than they need to.
friendship_ending.002: I have checked. There is no record of tonight. Nobody submitted one. It has not had time to become old yet.
friendship_ending.003: Daniel is already digging in his pocket. He pulls out a square of expired instant film, a little bent at one corner.
friendship_ending.004: Daniel is already digging through the front desk drawer, and comes up with the old instant camera and a single square of film.
friendship_ending.005: Then here. Scan this. It's the only record we've got.
friendship_ending.006: He lays it on the glass of the terminal. Nine people, badly framed, laughing at something none of them can remember.
friendship_ending.009: OWNERS: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
friendship_ending.011: For six years, every record I kept had someone missing from it. Someone I could not name.
friendship_ending.012: This one has nobody missing. I did not know a record could look like this.
friendship_ending.013: In the terminal's slot, a card of glass begins to glow. The photograph surfaces inside it slowly, like something rising through water.
friendship_ending.014: It comes out warm. Somehow it comes out warm.
friendship_ending.015: I said I'd cry at it. I'm crying at it. Nobody look at me.
friendship_ending.017: I know! It's fine! It's a happy one!
friendship_ending.018: Okay, but who keeps it? There's one card. There are nine of us.
friendship_ending.019: A rotation. A week each. And before anyone says no—
friendship_ending.020: Nobody says no. For the first time all night, nobody says no to the schedule.
friendship_ending.021: …Oh. Okay. Wow. It feels different when people agree.
friendship_ending.023: You're the one who always leaves, right? So if you have it, you have to come back. To hand it over. That's the rule.
friendship_ending.024: Eight people look at you. Nobody is teasing. It's the way people look at someone when they're handing them something that matters.
friendship_ending.025: "Then I'll come back. That's a promise."
friendship_ending.026: It's in the schedule now. Songha wrote it down. It's legally binding.
friendship_ending.027: "One week, and then I'm fighting Songha for a second week."
friendship_ending.029: Take the card in both hands, and hold it like it might still be warm tomorrow.
friendship_ending.030: It is. You don't know that yet. But it is.
friendship_ending.031: The Archive Wall has begun to dim, box by box, from the top down. Nobody needs to be told what that means.
friendship_ending.032: Thanks for keeping my stuff, ECHO. Even the embarrassing stuff.
friendship_ending.033: Thank you. Really. It was a good screening.
friendship_ending.034: Sleep well, okay? You earned it. Best building ever.
friendship_ending.035: You kept the light on for a long time. Somebody should notice that. {p}We noticed.
friendship_ending.036: Afterwards, without the lights, the building is just a building. You climb the stairs by phone torch, all nine of you, back to the roof.
friendship_ending.037: The sky over Mapo has gone the colour of peach tea left out overnight. Somewhere, a bus is starting its first route.
friendship_ending.038: My phone's dead. Again. Does anyone—
friendship_ending.039: Hanbi hands him the battery pack without looking. The battery pack does a full lap of the roof before it comes back to him, with a little less charge.
friendship_ending.040: New schedule. Nothing until noon. That's it. That's the whole schedule.
friendship_ending.043: Numbers! Everyone! I'm making a group chat. It's called "Stuck-in-a-Talking-Building Friends."
friendship_ending.044: I'm renaming it "Ghost and Eight Others."
friendship_ending.045: I'm pinning a schedule to it. Don't mute it.
friendship_ending.046: Your phone buzzes once. Then eight more times, in a row, like a small applause.
friendship_ending.047: Nine names in a list. You have never been in a group chat you didn't leave within a year. You look at this one for a long moment.
friendship_ending.048: Then, one at a time, they take your phone and save themselves into it properly.
friendship_ending.049: Songha saves himself as "Songha (schedule)." Daniel saves himself as "Daniel ★ Leader ★" and Justin changes it to "Daniel" before the phone comes back.
friendship_ending.050: Hanbi's contact has no note at all. Just his name, and a small drawing of a pencil where the photo would go.
friendship_ending.051: I saved myself as "Charlie (youngest, not my fault)." For legal reasons.
friendship_ending.052: The sun comes up over the rooftops of Mapo.
friendship_ending.053: Nine people stand at the edge of a building that won't exist next week, squinting at it like it's the first sunrise ever made.
friendship_ending.054: Nobody says anything clever. Hyunjun is still crying a bit. Justin is doing one slow, silly spin. Haruta is humming something that isn't from any film.
friendship_ending.055: That would be a good last shot. If this were a film.
friendship_ending.056: It isn't the last one, though.
friendship_ending.058: The glass card is in your coat pocket. You keep touching it, the way you check for keys. It is still, somehow, a little warm.
friendship_ending.059: Down in the alley, a van pulls up. Renovation crew. It's time to go.
friendship_ending.060: Breakfast? Right now? There's a place by the station that does—
friendship_ending.061: Next week. It's on the schedule. Go home, sleep.
friendship_ending.062: Next week, then. I'm holding everyone to it. I'm writing it on my other hand.
friendship_ending.063: I'm sleeping until two. Nobody text me until two. Actually, text me. I want the texts.
friendship_ending.065: He says it the way people say it when they mean the next time is already real. Not a door closing. A door propped open with a shoe.
friendship_ending.068: "See you next week. It's on Songha's schedule."
friendship_ending.069: Finally. Someone who reads the schedule.
friendship_ending.070: Hold up the glass card, just a little. Proof.
friendship_ending.072: And then it's everyone at once, overlapping, on the stairs, in the alley, under the laundromat's light.
friendship_ending.073: Text when you get home. So we know.
friendship_ending.074: See you, {{playerName}}. Next week. I'll pick the film, if we watch one. I already know which.
friendship_ending.075: See you! See you! I'm saying it twice so it counts double!
friendship_ending.076: You have always been the one who leaves. You're leaving now, down the stairs, past the laundromat, out into the morning.
friendship_ending.077: But it's different. You know exactly where you're coming back to.

newmem_group.017: Hamin slides a grape soda across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell grape soda. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.018: Hamin slides a black coffee across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell coffee. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.019: You were going to forget to drink anything. You always do when it's loud.

newmem_group.023: Mine. Still mine. It's been one week exactly.
newmem_group.024: Then you have to hand it over. That was the rule.
newmem_group.025: You put it on the table between the tteokbokki and the charger. Nine people, badly framed, laughing, catching the restaurant light.
newmem_group.026: New rule. Whoever has it next has to host. Which means another dinner. Which means next week. Which means—
newmem_group.027: Which means we just keep doing this forever?
newmem_group.029: By the door, Daniel has found a claw machine the size of a fridge. He has already spent four thousand won on it.
newmem_group.030: It's a different claw machine. It's a *new* claw machine. The old grudge doesn't apply.
newmem_group.032: Five times to a *new* machine. That's a fresh start.
newmem_group.033: The food arrives, too hot and too much. Somebody knocks over a cup. Somebody starts laughing and can't stop.
newmem_group.034: It isn't a memory yet. It's just Tuesday. You stay until they close.

hamin_ch1.001: Halfway down the stairs, the speakers click back on.

hamin_ch1.003: I did not want anyone to be late. I appear to have made everyone early instead.

hamin_ch1.032: If it were Songha's he'd have come back for it within the hour. With a form.
hamin_ch1.033: He writes, in small square capitals: PENCIL CASE. OWNER WAS NERVOUS BEFORE SOMETHING. IT PROBABLY WENT FINE.
hamin_ch1.034: Then seven gloves, none of which has ever met the others.
hamin_ch1.035: Seven people went home with one cold hand.
hamin_ch1.036: And nobody came back. You'd think one of them would come back.

hamin_ch1.038: GLOVE, LEFT. GREY. OWNER STILL HAS THE RIGHT ONE. IS HOPING.
hamin_ch1.039: An umbrella that opens inside out. A harmonica with a name scratched off. A keyring torch the size of a thumb.

hamin_ch1.041: Six years in a box. Still on.

hamin_ch1.044: Write: TORCH. STILL WORKS. HAS BEEN WAITING IN THE DARK, WHICH IS IRONIC.

hamin_ch2.001: There is a bass line coming through the ceiling of the lobby. It has been there for a while, in the way a headache is there before you name it.

hamin_ch2.004: Hamin. {{playerName}}. Good timing. We need bodies.
hamin_ch2.005: We need one body. It's a wave. With two people it's a ripple.
hamin_ch2.007: The farewell piece. For the building. Eight counts. Very emotional. I've been working on it for nine minutes.
hamin_ch2.008: It's good. We've run it six times. One more. I'm aware I've said that six times as well.

hamin_ch2.046: I like corn tea. That's not a fine. That's a reward.
hamin_ch2.047: You pay it to me. I pour it out.

hamin_ch2.051: I know. Eight counts. Then you can go back to everyone else.

haruta_final.001: You say it. *Haruta's.* It comes out fast, before you can dress it.
haruta_final.002: Selection received. RECORD 06. Preparing the card. This takes one minute. I am told a minute is long enough for most things.

haruta_ending_someday.027: …Specifically. {p} All right. I needed a second. I've had it.

haruta_ending_someday.034: I don't want you to be what I practise on. I want to be good at it by the time it's you.

haruta_ending_someday.042: You always left in spring. I'd like to be standing here when it arrives, and see you coming up the street.

justin_ch1.001: Every route through this building passes the front desk. That was the whole idea of the front desk.
justin_ch1.002: Justin has walked past it all night. This time he stops, and puts both elbows on the counter, and leans over to look at the side customers never see.
justin_ch1.004: Smaller than it looks. There's a heater under the desk that only warms your left foot.
justin_ch1.006: The right one learns to cope.
justin_ch1.007: The counter flap sticks. It always did. You lift, then push, and it swings up the way it swung up a hundred nights one winter.
justin_ch1.008: Your hands knew how before you'd decided to try.
justin_ch1.009: You didn't even look at it. I know what that is. That's a routine.
justin_ch1.010: Is there a book? There was a book. I had to write my name in a book.
justin_ch1.011: Second drawer from the bottom. It needs a hip, not a hand. You give it the hip.
justin_ch1.012: Inside: a stapler, a dead torch, a ring of keys with a cracked plastic 25 on the tag — and a green hardback ledger, soft at the corners.
justin_ch1.013: ROOM HIRE, it says on the cover, in marker. Underneath, in a different marker: *please write clearly. please.*
justin_ch1.014: That's it. That's the book. I'm in there somewhere.
justin_ch1.015: February. Three years ago. I want to see what I wrote. I was so nervous I think I spelled my own name wrong.
justin_ch1.016: "Easy. We look for the worst handwriting."
justin_ch1.017: Rude. Accurate. My sevens look like ones and my ones look like accidents.
justin_ch1.018: He flips pages fast, the way he does everything, and overshoots February twice.
justin_ch1.019: "Tell me the date. I'll find the night."
justin_ch1.020: The ninth. No — the tenth, technically. It was after midnight.
justin_ch1.021: You turn the pages for him. Slowly. He watches your hands instead of the book.
justin_ch1.022: Turn straight to the page with the coffee ring.
justin_ch1.023: February had a coffee ring on it. You put it there. You remember being annoyed at yourself for a week.
justin_ch1.024: You knew exactly where that was.
justin_ch1.025: I spilled on it. I felt terrible. It's a very easy month to find.
justin_ch1.026: And there it is. One line among a lot of lines.
justin_ch1.027: ROOM B. IN: 00:30. NAME: a J, and then a small, panicked scribble.
justin_ch1.028: PURPOSE: *dance*, crossed out. *practice*, crossed out. And then, pressed hard enough to dent the paper: *nothing*.

justin_ch1.031: Great plan. Flawless. Nobody came to look. Except the one person with the keys.
